key_insight: Synthetic EHR generators should undergo patient-level memorisation audits, since similarity heuristics and aggregate metrics can obscure privacy risks.
clinical_relevance: These audits could help assess whether synthetic clinical records expose information memorised from individual patients.
method: Compare membership-inference evaluations across four autoregressive EHR generators.
Test patient-trajectory reconstruction from partial context.
Use randomly assigned patient-level canaries to distinguish memorisation from clinical generalisation.
evidence_signal: In a GPT-2-style model deliberately overfit to 1,000 MIMIC-IV patient trajectories, training-patient canaries were systematically recovered and reconstruction approached perfect accuracy as context increased, unlike held-out patients.
watch_item: This deliberately overfit positive control demonstrates audit sensitivity, not the prevalence of memorisation in realistically trained models.
paper_title: Synthetic EHR Generators Should Be Audited Like LLMs
